h: Making a Digbeth night of it
p: Golf Fang is an 18+ adults-only venue, so it's firmly a grown-up night out rather than a family day. Plan your evening around a booked tee time and work outwards from there. A popular shape is food first, golf in the middle and then a wander round Digbeth's bars once your scorecard's settled the arguments. Eat beforehand if you're not planning to dine there, as nobody putts well on an empty stomach.

A few house rules make the round more fun for everyone. Agree any side bets or forfeits before the first hole, keep the group moving so you're not holding up the next lot, and appoint one honest person to keep score. If you've got a big group, splitting into smaller teams keeps the pace up and stops the banter from fading as people wait their turn.

The Custard Factory itself is worth a nosey, with its colourful murals, independent shops and creative studios in the old Bird's Custard buildings. Digbeth's walls are covered in street art, so bring your phone for photos as you walk in. When you're ready to head home or move on, Birmingham Moor Street station is a short walk away, and the Bullring and New Street are just beyond that. Weekend nights round here are lively, so keep an eye on last trains and book taxis early if you can.
